why: Turning a loop into a full track by saying 'build up and drop, make the break longer' is the core of our north star, and the design keeps the edits small, named and one-undo, which is exactly what chat-DAW users ask for.
notes: Competitors now do this too, so it's expected, not unique: Veena's CoProducer (Sep 2026) plans sections and parts in a browser DAW, VIXSOUND arranges 'intro 8, build 16, drop' inside Ableton, and Suno Studio 2.0 (Aug 2026) arranges from its chat bar. Our edge is voice and Hinglish, artist-shaped layouts (Bodzin, Böhmer, Afterlife) and Keys saying what changed in musical words. Lead with those in the demo and the reply text.

Watch speed and trust. The prompt grows 40% and one run took 9.5 s (over the 8 s bar). The DAWZY study found people rate 'control' lowest, so keep the executor's own line ('Break 2 is now 24 bars') and the mini song map. Re-measure the timing at build and trim the prompt before adding more examples.

Mismatches with UX-1 that AI-1 should settle with song.js: (1) the template's parts differ (Outro drums+pad here vs drums+chords in UX-1; Break here drops kick and bass, UX-1 drops all drums; UX-1's template sets no transitions). Keep one table in songTemplate. (2) 'vary' per section needs a way to generate into pattern B, but UX-1 says generators only write pattern A; ask for a helper (for example songMakeUnique, then write to the variant). (3) Use only the song.js names (songMode, songLoop, songMakeUnique, songFlash), not both spellings.
improve: Agree one 'the break' rule with UX-1: the playing one, else the last touched, else the first (UX-1's songFind uses the last break).
Put transitionEvents in song.js (or groove.js), not actions.js, so playback and export don't depend on assistant code.
Drop the bubble's Undo; UX-1's toolbar chip already gives it.
